frameworks.name: NIST CSF 2.0
frameworks.description: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 organized around governance and lifecycle functions for managing enterprise cyber risk.

categories.name: Identify
items: Maintain a current inventory of hardware, software, data, and third-party dependencies.
Document business context, mission-critical services, and risk tolerance for the data centre.
Map data flows between DMZ, management, production, backup, and external connectivity zones.
Classify assets by sensitivity, regulatory scope, and operational criticality.
Assess supply chain exposure for hosted platforms, MSPs, and security tooling.

categories.name: Protect
items: Enforce role-based access control and MFA for all administrative interfaces.
Implement network segmentation, DMZ controls, and least-privilege firewall policies.
Apply secure configuration baselines for servers, virtualization, and network devices.
Protect backups, secrets, and cryptographic material with rotation and recovery procedures.
Deliver user, operator, and engineering awareness training aligned to privileged workflows.

categories.name: Detect
items: Centralize security logs from firewalls, PAM, operating systems, and cloud services.
Define detection content for brute force, privilege escalation, suspicious east-west traffic, and data exfiltration.
Continuously monitor vulnerabilities, configuration drift, and malware indicators.
Tune alert thresholds and establish triage workflows with documented ownership.
Validate detections with purple-team exercises and incident simulations.

categories.name: Respond
items: Maintain incident playbooks for ransomware, insider threat, DDoS, and credential misuse.
Define communications paths for executives, legal, IT operations, and external responders.
Contain compromised accounts, endpoints, and network segments using approved procedures.
Capture evidence, preserve logs, and document timelines for post-incident analysis.
Coordinate eradication tasks, access resets, and stakeholder updates during active response.

categories.name: Recover
items: Restore services from tested backups with integrity validation and rollback plans.
Track lessons learned and update architecture, detections, and runbooks after incidents.
Rebuild trust boundaries, credentials, and secrets affected during compromise.
Measure recovery against RTO and RPO targets for critical services.
Communicate recovery status and residual risk to business owners and auditors.

frameworks.name: CIS Controls v8
frameworks.description: Prioritized safeguards for foundational cyber hygiene and continuous risk reduction.

categories.name: 1. Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
items: Maintain an authorized asset inventory.
Detect unmanaged or rogue devices on network segments.

categories.name: 2. Inventory and Control of Software Assets
items: Track approved software and versions.
Block or remediate unauthorized software promptly.

categories.name: 3. Data Protection
items: Classify sensitive data and retention needs.
Apply encryption, backup, and exfiltration controls.

categories.name: 4. Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software
items: Apply hardened baselines to servers and endpoints.
Continuously monitor for configuration drift.

categories.name: 5. Account Management
items: Review account lifecycle events.
Disable stale, shared, or orphaned accounts.

categories.name: 6. Access Control Management
items: Enforce least privilege and role reviews.
Require MFA for remote and privileged access.

categories.name: 7. Continuous Vulnerability Management
items: Scan systems routinely for vulnerabilities.
Prioritize remediation based on exploitability and criticality.

categories.name: 8. Audit Log Management
items: Centralize and protect security logs.
Establish retention and review procedures.

categories.name: 9. Email and Web Browser Protections
items: Harden browser and email security settings.
Block malicious content and unsafe attachments.

categories.name: 10. Malware Defenses
items: Deploy prevention and detection controls.
Validate response actions for malicious activity.

categories.name: 11. Data Recovery
items: Maintain offline and immutable backups.
Test restore procedures at defined intervals.

categories.name: 12. Network Infrastructure Management
items: Secure routers, switches, and firewalls.
Document changes and monitor network device health.

categories.name: 13. Network Monitoring and Defense
items: Inspect traffic for malicious patterns.
Segment high-value systems and monitor lateral movement.

categories.name: 14. Security Awareness and Skills Training
items: Train staff on phishing, access handling, and reporting.
Develop technical training for administrators and responders.

categories.name: 15. Service Provider Management
items: Assess third-party security obligations.
Monitor provider access and performance against contracts.

categories.name: 16. Application Software Security
items: Integrate security testing into delivery workflows.
Protect secrets and dependencies in build pipelines.

categories.name: 17. Incident Response Management
items: Maintain and exercise response plans.
Capture lessons learned and update procedures.

categories.name: 18. Penetration Testing
items: Perform regular internal and external assessments.
Track remediation for discovered weaknesses.

frameworks.name: ISO 27001:2022
frameworks.description: Information security management system standard with Annex A control themes spanning organizational, people, physical, and technological measures.

categories.name: A.5 Organizational Controls
items: Define security policies and ownership.
Manage supplier, project, and asset governance controls.

categories.name: A.6 People Controls
items: Screen personnel and define responsibilities.
Train staff and manage disciplinary and termination processes.

categories.name: A.7 Physical Controls
items: Restrict physical entry to data halls.
Protect equipment against theft, tampering, and environmental threats.

categories.name: A.8 Technological Controls
items: Implement endpoint, network, and application safeguards.
Protect logs, identities, data, and backups.

categories.name: Asset Management
items: Assign ownership for information assets.
Handle asset return, disposal, and labeling.

categories.name: Access Control
items: Control user registration and privilege grants.
Review privileged access and authentication practices.

categories.name: Cryptography
items: Define encryption policies and key management.
Protect data in transit and at rest.

categories.name: Operations Security
items: Manage changes, malware protection, and backups.
Separate environments and monitor capacity.

categories.name: Communications Security
items: Secure network services and information transfer.
Segment networks based on trust and sensitivity.

categories.name: System Acquisition and Development
items: Include security requirements in projects.
Manage vulnerabilities in development and release processes.

categories.name: Supplier Relationships
items: Contract for security requirements with suppliers.
Monitor service delivery and third-party changes.

categories.name: Incident Management
items: Report, classify, and respond to events.
Collect evidence and learn from incidents.

categories.name: Business Continuity
items: Embed information security into continuity planning.
Test recovery and crisis communication arrangements.

categories.name: Compliance
items: Meet legal, regulatory, and audit obligations.
Protect records and privacy-related information.

frameworks.name: HIPAA Security Rule
frameworks.description: Safeguards for protecting electronic protected health information through administrative, physical, and technical controls.

categories.name: Administrative Safeguards
items: Perform periodic risk analysis for systems storing or processing ePHI.
Assign a security officer and define workforce security responsibilities.
Authorize, supervise, and review workforce access to ePHI systems.
Establish contingency plans, backup procedures, and emergency-mode operations.

categories.name: Physical Safeguards
items: Control facility access to server rooms and records areas.
Protect workstations and restrict unauthorized device use.
Track device and media movement, disposal, reuse, and accountability.
Implement environmental and physical protections for critical infrastructure.

categories.name: Technical Safeguards
items: Assign unique user IDs and emergency access procedures.
Implement audit controls for systems handling ePHI.
Protect integrity of ePHI against improper alteration or destruction.
Secure data in transit with encryption and trusted channel controls.

frameworks.name: PCI-DSS v4.0
frameworks.description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard requirements for protecting cardholder data environments.

categories.name: 1. Install and Maintain Network Security Controls
items: Document firewall and router standards.
Restrict inbound and outbound traffic to required flows only.

categories.name: 2. Apply Secure Configurations to All System Components
items: Remove vendor defaults and unnecessary services.
Harden systems before they enter production.

categories.name: 3. Protect Stored Account Data
items: Minimize stored account data.
Render PAN unreadable with strong cryptography and key controls.

categories.name: 4. Protect Cardholder Data with Strong Cryptography During Transmission
items: Encrypt transmission over open or public networks.
Validate certificate and protocol posture.

categories.name: 5. Protect All Systems and Networks from Malicious Software
items: Deploy anti-malware where appropriate.
Detect, alert, and respond to malware events.

categories.name: 6. Develop and Maintain Secure Systems and Software
items: Track vulnerabilities and patch in defined windows.
Use secure development and change control practices.

categories.name: 7. Restrict Access to System Components and Cardholder Data by Business Need to Know
items: Define roles and least-privilege access.
Review access assignments regularly.

categories.name: 8. Identify Users and Authenticate Access to System Components
items: Use unique IDs and strong authentication.
Protect service, application, and privileged accounts.

categories.name: 9. Restrict Physical Access to Cardholder Data
items: Secure facilities, racks, and media.
Log and review visitor and physical access events.

categories.name: 10. Log and Monitor All Access to System Components and Cardholder Data
items: Collect, protect, and review audit logs.
Synchronize time and alert on suspicious events.

categories.name: 11. Test Security of Systems and Networks Regularly
items: Run vulnerability scans and penetration tests.
Validate IDS/IPS, file integrity, and segmentation controls.

categories.name: 12. Support Information Security with Organizational Policies and Programs
items: Maintain governance, awareness, and incident response processes.
Review security policy, risk, and third-party obligations regularly.
